newsitem.title: LEBANON: Saudi prince builds $33 mln Beirut hotel.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince builds $33 mln Beirut hotel.

text.p: A Saudi prince laid the foundation stone on Tuesday of a $33 million luxury hotel in central Beirut to be managed by the Inter-Continental Hotels Corporation.
Construction of the Beirut Forum Hotel in the city centre being redeveloped by Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, is planned to start in June and finish at the end of 1998.
The Lebanese Arab Hotels Corporation, a Saudi-Lebanese joint venture, said the cost of the project was $33 million. It is being built on land bought from Solidere in 1995.
Saudi Prince Husam Bin Saud Bin Abdelaziz, chairman of the corporation, and Lebanon's billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri laid the foundation stone together.

The hotel will comprise two separate seven-storey buildings with a total of 123 single and double rooms, 72 business suites, four executive suites, two royal suites, eight conference halls, two restaurants, a night club and a sports club.

"The idea of the project started two years ago when I received two separate offers, one of them to build a hotel in Beirut and the second to build a hotel in Paris, I preferred Beirut," the prince told Reuters.
He said Lebanon was an encouraging place for the hotel industry but suffered a shortage of hotels.
"I chose Beirut because it is a booming place, on the start line of building growth, and because I have learned that Lebanon has only 7,000 hotel rooms while it needs 40,000 rooms," the prince added.
